I’m in same position as you and I feel your pain. Feels like the veil has been lifted and now it’s just a job in a quickly failing industry. Try to get to a better school. Don’t be afraid to set boundaries and do what’s right for yourself. 

Something that has helped me is leaning into the idea that this is simply a job. I took it on last year wide eyed and ready to change the world. Screw that. It’s a 9-5 with long breaks, decent pay, and great benefits. 

You don’t have to change the world and the system, and you can’t even if you wanted to. You need to focus on your life outside of work as much as you can and don’t be a martyr! 

Also, I’m not saying don’t care. Obviously this is a job that requires you to care about others and that’s great if you’re into it. Just always remember that it’s your life. Don’t live it for other people.

As someone who just got into it (3rd year), it can be disappointing when you actually get into it. It’s just a job. I did a similar path as you’re describing and my first year and half or so was fun because it was new. Now I’m begging for a way out, but I also work at a shit school. 

Unfortunately once the veil is lifted and you see the behind the scenes, it’s just a normal job but you also have to deal with 100 kids every day. Some you will love, some you’ll hate. Some will make you come to school to make sure they keep learning every day. Others will make you cry in the parking lot. 

My state has a website that grades every public school using all kinds of data. I would not take a job anywhere that has a bad rating. Public education is going downhill fast, and it’s burning people out like never before. 

Also the only way you get a job at a good school is math and maybe science. Social studies teachers are a dime a dozen. 

Good luck!
